pages.title: AI Interview Assistant Features | OfferSteady
pages.description: Explore OfferSteady features for live transcription, resume-grounded interview guidance, screenshot questions, written exams, and review.
pages.h1: AI interview guidance for preparation and live sessions.
pages.intro: OfferSteady combines an English Web workspace with a desktop Companion so you can prepare context, follow a conversation, request guidance, and review the session in one workflow.

sections.heading: What does the AI interview assistant do?
paragraphs: OfferSteady turns live interview audio, typed questions, and user-triggered screenshots into structured guidance. Before a session, you choose the resume, job description, and optional knowledge materials that are relevant. During the session, the Web workspace displays interviewer and candidate transcripts separately and can prepare a Quick Answer when you request one or enable Auto Answer.

The product does not replace your judgement or make an unverified claim true. Treat every response as a draft: check the facts, adapt the language to your natural speaking style, and answer from experience you can support.

sections.heading: How are answers grounded in your materials?
paragraphs: A session uses only the materials you select. Resume and job-description context help the assistant focus on the role, while optional knowledge collections can provide project or domain information. The answer view keeps source provenance visible where available so you can distinguish selected material from generated guidance.
Grounding improves relevance, but it is not a guarantee of accuracy. Review names, dates, metrics, technical details, and responsibilities before using a suggestion.

sections.heading: Which workflows are available?
paragraphs: Realtime interview guidance follows live audio from the connected Companion. Screen Assist handles a screen region that you deliberately capture. Written Exam mode removes the audio workflow and keeps screenshot-based assistance. Interview Review brings together confirmed questions, guidance, transcripts, and source context after a session.

OfferSteady is designed for English-language use across the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia. Device and meeting compatibility still depends on the operating system, permissions, audio route, and interview platform.

sections.heading: How do you choose the right input?
paragraphs: Use live transcription when the interview is happening on a supported computer and you want to follow the conversation as it develops. Use a typed question when audio is unavailable or when you want to restate a question precisely. Use Screen Assist only for material that is visible on your selected screen and that you are permitted to capture.

Each input has a different limitation. Speech recognition can revise a partial sentence, typed text reflects exactly what you enter, and a screenshot may omit content outside the captured region. Check the original question before deciding that the guidance addresses it.

sections.heading: What should you check before relying on an answer?
paragraphs: First confirm that the recognised question matches what the interviewer asked. Then check every reference to your resume, employer, project, date, metric, tool, or responsibility. Remove anything you cannot defend and shorten wording that does not sound natural when spoken.

For a technical answer, also check assumptions, constraints, trade-offs, failure handling, and whether the requested programming language is selected. For a behavioural answer, make your own action distinct from the team's work and keep the result tied to evidence you actually have.

sections.heading: Use OfferSteady responsibly
paragraphs: Follow the interview organiser's rules for AI assistance, recording, screen capture, confidentiality, and external tools. Obtain consent where required. OfferSteady should help you organise what you already know, not present invented experience or confidential information as your own.

pages.title: AI Interview Assistant | OfferSteady
pages.description: Learn how OfferSteady combines selected interview context, live questions, typed prompts, and screenshots into responsible answer guidance.
pages.h1: Keep interview guidance connected to your real experience.
pages.intro: OfferSteady helps candidates organise relevant context and turn a live or written question into a response structure they can verify and express in their own words.

sections.heading: What is an AI interview assistant?
paragraphs: An AI interview assistant is a tool that helps a candidate interpret questions, organise evidence, and prepare a clear response. OfferSteady supports this workflow with selected resumes, job descriptions, knowledge materials, typed questions, realtime transcripts, and screenshots. It produces guidance rather than speaking for the candidate or guaranteeing an outcome.

The most useful output is specific enough to organise an answer but cautious enough to preserve the candidate's judgement. That is why OfferSteady asks users to verify every claim and keep answers faithful to their actual responsibilities, decisions, results, and lessons.

sections.heading: How does session context work?
paragraphs: You choose the material for each interview before the live session starts. A resume can establish the experience you want to discuss, a job description can identify the role's priorities, and a knowledge collection can add selected project or domain details. Nothing should be treated as verified merely because it appears in a generated response.
Separating session context also reduces irrelevant material. If the role changes, create or update the session selection rather than assuming that one answer profile fits every interview.

sections.heading: When should you use manual or automatic answers?
paragraphs: Manual Quick Answer keeps the candidate in control: confirm that a real interviewer question has been recognised, then request guidance. Auto Answer can react to confirmed interviewer questions when enabled, but it remains optional and can be turned off. Typed questions are useful when audio is unavailable or when a clarification needs to be entered directly.
Whichever mode you choose, read the suggestion critically. Correct factual errors, remove claims you cannot support, and use the structure as a prompt for your own response.

sections.heading: How do you prepare evidence for a session?
paragraphs: Read the job description and identify a small set of responsibilities that matter for this interview. For each one, choose an example you can explain without notes: the situation, your decision, the work you personally completed, the result, and what you learned. Update the selected resume or knowledge material when a fact is missing rather than expecting the model to infer it.

Keep source material focused. A concise project summary with accurate names, dates, constraints, and outcomes is more useful than a large collection of unrelated documents. Do not add confidential employer information or personal data that the interview does not require.

sections.heading: How should generated guidance be adapted?
paragraphs: Start with the direct answer, then choose only the evidence relevant to the question. Replace generic phrases with details you can verify and remove recommendations that do not match your role. If the question asks for an opinion, explain the principle and trade-off behind your choice instead of presenting one approach as universally correct.

A suggestion may be too long for a live conversation. Use the opening and key evidence as a speaking outline, listen for follow-up questions, and answer those follow-ups directly. The goal is a clearer version of your own reasoning, not a script that hides uncertainty.

sections.heading: Responsible-use boundary
paragraphs: Interview rules differ by employer, assessment, and jurisdiction. Confirm whether AI assistance, recording, transcription, or screen capture is permitted. Do not upload trade secrets, unrelated personal data, or material you do not have the right to process.

pages.title: Real-Time Interview Guidance | OfferSteady
pages.description: See how OfferSteady uses a connected desktop Companion, progressive transcription, speaker roles, and selected context during live interviews.
pages.h1: Follow live interview questions without losing the conversation.
pages.intro: The desktop Companion sends the audio sources you enable to the active session, while the Web workspace shows progressive transcripts and prepares guidance around confirmed interviewer questions.

sections.heading: How does live interview guidance work?
paragraphs: OfferSteady separates microphone audio from supported computer-output audio so the Web workspace can label candidate and interviewer speech. Progressive transcription can change while a sentence is still being recognised; confirmed turns are retained in the conversation history. The assistant uses confirmed interviewer questions together with the context selected for that session.

You can request a Quick Answer manually or enable Auto Answer for confirmed questions. Automatic mode is optional, and neither mode changes the requirement to verify the final suggestion before using it.

sections.heading: What do you need before a session?
paragraphs: Install and open the compatible desktop Companion, grant only the permissions required by the feature, choose the correct microphone and computer-output source, and connect it with the code shown in the preparation page. Confirm that the selected audio meters respond before entering a live interview.

Audio availability depends on the operating system, device route, headset state, conferencing software, and permissions. Changing an output device during a session can require the Companion to recover or reconnect the capture route.

sections.heading: What happens to audio and transcripts?
paragraphs: Raw audio is not stored by default. Audio frames are processed for the active transcription path. Session records and supported transcript data follow the controls described in the Privacy Policy and product interface. Avoid capturing conversations unless you have the required permission or consent.

sections.heading: Why can a live transcript change?
paragraphs: Speech recognition first produces a partial interpretation of the current phrase. That text can grow or be corrected as more audio arrives. A confirmed turn is more stable, but background noise, overlapping speakers, accents, specialised names, and an incorrect audio source can still reduce accuracy.

Use the speaker labels and the original conversation together. If the displayed interviewer question is incomplete, wait for the confirmed turn, enter the question manually, or ask the interviewer to repeat it. Do not treat a partial transcript as a final record.

sections.heading: How do you recover from an audio-route change?
paragraphs: If you connect or remove a headset, switch meeting software, or change the computer's output device, check the Companion's selected sources and meters again. The operating system can move audio to a different route even when the meeting continues normally. Re-select the intended source before assuming that transcription has failed.

If a meter remains inactive, verify the relevant operating-system permission and confirm that another application is not using an unexpected input. Keep the Web session open while restoring the device route, then confirm that new speech appears before requesting guidance.

sections.heading: What should you expect from AI guidance?
paragraphs: Network conditions, speech recognition, model providers, device permissions, and source material can introduce delay or mistakes. Keep listening to the interviewer, ask for clarification when necessary, and do not rely on OfferSteady as the sole means of completing an interview.

pages.title: Screen Assist for Interview Questions | OfferSteady
pages.description: Use OfferSteady Screen Assist for user-selected coding, system-design, chart, or written questions with visible answer guidance.
pages.h1: Turn a selected screen region into structured answer guidance.
pages.intro: Screen Assist captures only the region you choose through the desktop Companion and sends it to the active session for question understanding and answer guidance.

sections.heading: What can Screen Assist help with?
paragraphs: Screen Assist can help organise coding prompts, system-design diagrams, charts, multiple-step written questions, and other visible material. For programming tasks, the session's chosen programming language can guide the code example. The response can include an approach, assumptions, complexity, implementation, or explanation depending on what is visible.

Image recognition can miss small text, cropped constraints, hidden context, or diagram details. Capture the complete question region, then compare the response with the original prompt before relying on it.

sections.heading: How is a screenshot created?
paragraphs: A screenshot is user-triggered. Opening the website does not start screen capture. From the Companion, choose the intended display or region and use the capture control or configured shortcut. The image is associated with the connected session so the answer can appear in the correct Web workspace.
Do not capture unrelated private messages, credentials, personal information, or confidential employer material. Follow assessment rules and obtain permission where required.

sections.heading: How should coding answers be reviewed?
paragraphs: Check that the solution matches the requested language, input and output format, constraints, edge cases, and complexity requirements. Run or reason through representative examples. A syntactically complete answer can still misunderstand the problem, so confirm the algorithm before using the code.

sections.heading: How do you capture a readable question?
paragraphs: Include the complete prompt, visible constraints, examples, diagrams, labels, and any language requirement. Avoid a capture that cuts off the bottom of a question or includes so much unrelated screen content that the important text becomes too small. If a prompt spans multiple areas, capture the part needed for the current answer and provide missing context through the available question controls.

Before triggering Screen Assist, close or move private messages, credentials, personal information, and unrelated documents out of the selected region. The visible region is the input; content outside it cannot be assumed and content inside it may be processed for the requested answer.

sections.heading: How do different question types change the review?
paragraphs: For a system-design diagram, verify labels, capacity assumptions, boundaries, and failure paths. For a chart or table, confirm units, axes, time ranges, and whether the question asks for description or interpretation. For a written response, compare the answer with every requested subpart and word or format constraint.

If recognition is uncertain, recapture a clearer region instead of building on a mistaken premise. Treat generated explanations and code as drafts, and use only reasoning that you understand well enough to explain or defend.

sections.heading: Screen Assist is guidance
paragraphs: OfferSteady does not guarantee that a screenshot is complete or that generated code will pass every case. Use the result as a structured aid, explain only reasoning you understand, and comply with the organiser's rules for external assistance.

pages.intro: After a session, OfferSteady brings the conversation record and generated guidance into one review so you can check accuracy and prepare for the next round.

sections.heading: What appears in an interview review?
paragraphs: A review can include confirmed interviewer and candidate transcript turns, recognised questions, answer guidance, screenshot answers, and the source context associated with the session. The exact record depends on which features were used and which items were retained by the active product controls.

Review is most useful when you compare the transcript with your memory rather than treating it as a perfect record. Speech recognition can omit or revise words, especially when audio quality is poor, speakers overlap, or a device route changes.

sections.heading: How can review improve preparation?
paragraphs: Identify questions where your answer lacked a clear example, measurable result, technical trade-off, or concise opening. Turn those gaps into a preparation checklist. Update your resume or knowledge materials only with information you can verify, then practise a shorter version in your own words.

For technical questions, check whether the explanation covered assumptions, alternatives, complexity, failure modes, and testing. For behavioural questions, confirm that the situation, action, and result reflect your actual role.

sections.heading: Can session content be exported or deleted?
paragraphs: Supported review content can be exported or managed through the controls available in the product. Data availability and retention are described in the Privacy Policy. Contact support when the available controls do not address an access, correction, or deletion request.

sections.heading: What should you review first?
paragraphs: Begin with the questions that changed direction, required clarification, or produced an answer you found difficult to deliver. Compare the confirmed transcript with your memory of the conversation. Mark recognition errors separately from answer-quality issues so that an audio problem is not mistaken for a preparation gap.

Then review the opening sentence, evidence, trade-offs, and conclusion of each important response. Look for unsupported metrics, vague ownership, missing constraints, or an answer that reached the point too late. Convert each observation into one specific practice task for the next interview.

sections.heading: How can you build a reusable preparation loop?
paragraphs: After review, update only verified source facts. Create a shorter project summary, add a missing decision or result, and remove old details that no longer reflect your experience. Rehearse the same evidence against a different question so you learn the underlying story rather than memorising one answer.

Technical candidates can record assumptions, alternatives, complexity, tests, and failure modes they omitted. Behavioural candidates can separate personal contribution from team activity and prepare a concise result. Future guidance can then start from clearer material without changing what actually happened.

sections.heading: Keep sensitive information minimal
paragraphs: Do not retain or share confidential interview content unless you are authorised to do so. Remove unnecessary personal data before contacting support, and never send passwords or verification codes.

pages.title: Interview Preparation Guides | OfferSteady
pages.description: Use OfferSteady interview preparation guidance to organise real examples, role context, device setup, and responsible AI-assisted practice.
pages.h1: Prepare evidence before you prepare wording.
pages.intro: Strong interview preparation starts with the role, the question's intent, and examples you can defend. These principles help you prepare before using live guidance.

sections.heading: How should you prepare your interview context?
paragraphs: Start with the current job description. List the capabilities the role repeatedly asks for, then match each one to a real project, decision, result, or lesson from your experience. Choose the resume version that best represents those examples and remove outdated or unsupported claims.

Use optional knowledge materials for concise project facts, domain definitions, or reusable evidence. Avoid uploading large unrelated document sets because more context does not automatically produce a better answer.

sections.heading: How should you structure a behavioural answer?
paragraphs: Open with the situation and goal in one or two sentences. Spend most of the answer on your actions, decisions, trade-offs, and collaboration. Close with a result you can verify and one lesson that influenced later work. If the interviewer follows up, answer the new question directly instead of repeating the full story.
Practise multiple lengths. A short version helps you start clearly, while a longer version gives you evidence for follow-up questions.

sections.heading: How should you prepare for technical questions?
paragraphs: Separate definition, mechanism, trade-off, example, and failure handling. For coding problems, clarify inputs and constraints before choosing a data structure or algorithm. For system design, state assumptions, estimate scale, define interfaces, and explain how the design behaves when dependencies fail.
Do not memorise a single standard answer. Interviewers often change constraints to understand how you reason.

sections.heading: How do you turn a job description into a practice plan?
paragraphs: Group repeated requirements into a few themes such as technical depth, ownership, communication, or customer impact. For each theme, write one primary example and one backup example. Note the evidence, the trade-off you made, and the follow-up question you would find hardest to answer.

Practise answering the question before polishing the wording. If the evidence is weak, choose a better example or acknowledge the limit. Do not add a metric, title, or responsibility simply because it would fit the role more neatly.

sections.heading: How should you practise follow-up questions?
paragraphs: After each prepared answer, ask what changed, what failed, what you would do differently, and how another stakeholder viewed the decision. Technical follow-ups may change scale, consistency, latency, cost, or security constraints. Behavioural follow-ups may test conflict, ownership, or learning.

Answer the new condition first. Reuse only the context that remains relevant, and say when an earlier assumption no longer holds. This makes the conversation clearer than repeating the full original story.

sections.heading: What should you check before a live session?
paragraphs: Open the desktop Companion, verify microphone and computer-output sources, confirm permissions, connect the session code, and test the visible meters. Keep a fallback plan for device or network problems. Follow the organiser's rules for AI tools, recording, screen capture, and confidential information.

Prepare the physical setup too. Use a stable network where possible, connect power, close unrelated notifications, and keep the interview link and a non-AI fallback note available. If you change a headset or output device, confirm the Companion route again before the interview begins.

pages.title: Interview Question Types and Frameworks | OfferSteady
pages.description: Understand behavioural, technical, coding, system-design, and follow-up interview questions and prepare evidence-based response frameworks.
pages.h1: Understand what the interviewer is trying to evaluate.
pages.intro: Question wording changes, but the underlying evaluation is often stable. Prepare the evidence and reasoning pattern behind each question type rather than memorising scripts.

sections.heading: What are behavioural interview questions evaluating?
paragraphs: Behavioural questions examine how you acted in a real situation: your ownership, judgement, communication, conflict handling, prioritisation, or learning. Choose an example where your contribution is clear. Explain the context briefly, describe the decisions you personally made, and connect the result to the capability the role requires.
If you cannot verify a metric, describe the observable outcome without inventing precision. A credible limitation is stronger than an impressive unsupported claim.

sections.heading: How should you answer technical concept questions?
paragraphs: Begin with a precise definition, then explain the mechanism and why it matters. Compare alternatives using relevant trade-offs such as consistency, latency, cost, complexity, security, or operability. Finish with a real example or failure mode when you have one.
When the question is ambiguous, state your interpretation and ask a clarifying question. This demonstrates scope control and prevents an answer to the wrong problem.

sections.heading: What is a good coding-question workflow?
paragraphs: Restate the problem, confirm inputs and outputs, identify constraints, and test a simple example. Explain a straightforward solution before optimising. Choose data structures deliberately, state time and space complexity, then test edge cases such as empty input, duplicates, limits, overflow, or invalid state.
Generated code is a draft. Confirm the requested language, syntax, library assumptions, and all hidden constraints before using it.

sections.heading: How should you approach a system-design question?
paragraphs: Clarify the users, core actions, scale, latency, consistency, availability, security, and cost expectations before drawing components. Define the main interfaces and data flow, then explain storage, caching, asynchronous work, failure handling, and observability at the level the interviewer requests.

There is rarely one correct architecture. State assumptions and compare alternatives. If the interviewer changes a constraint, identify which part of the design is affected and why instead of replacing the whole answer without explanation.

sections.heading: How do you handle a question you cannot answer fully?
paragraphs: State what you understand, identify the missing fact, and ask a focused clarification. If you know a related mechanism, explain the connection without pretending it is the same answer. A transparent boundary gives the interviewer a useful view of your reasoning and avoids an unsupported claim.

For an unfamiliar tool, reason from the problem it appears to solve and compare it with a system you know. Separate verified knowledge from your inference. OfferSteady guidance can also be incomplete, so apply the same standard to anything shown in the workspace.

sections.heading: How do follow-up questions change the answer?
paragraphs: A follow-up usually introduces a new constraint or asks for evidence behind an earlier claim. Address the changed condition first, preserve relevant context, and avoid repeating the full original response. If your earlier assumption is no longer valid, say so and explain the revised decision.

Listen for the exact dimension being tested. A request for more detail is different from disagreement, a new scale assumption, or a request for a concrete example. Confirm the change and then update only the affected part of your reasoning.

pages.title: Download the OfferSteady Desktop Companion
pages.description: Download the OfferSteady desktop Companion for supported macOS and Windows computers and review the setup steps before a session.
pages.h1: Connect interview audio and screenshots to your Web workspace.
pages.intro: The desktop Companion works with the OfferSteady Web session to capture only the audio sources and screen regions you enable.

actions.label: Start Free
actions.detail: Create or sign in to your account. Verified Companion release options appear in the interview preparation flow.

sections.heading: What does the desktop Companion do?
paragraphs: The Companion connects a supported macOS or Windows computer to the active Web workspace with a short connection code. It provides the device-side microphone, supported computer-output audio, and user-triggered screenshot capabilities required by live interview and written-exam workflows.

The Companion does not start a session by itself. Opening the website alone does not begin audio or screen capture. You choose the sources, grant operating-system permissions, and connect the intended session.

sections.heading: Which installer should you choose?
paragraphs: On macOS, choose the installer that matches Apple silicon or Intel hardware. On Windows, use the supported 64-bit installer. The download controls in the application show the currently published release options. Do not install packages copied from an unverified third-party source.

Keep the Companion updated when the preparation page reports that a newer compatible version is available. A stable application identity helps the operating system retain permissions, but macOS and Windows can still require the user to confirm microphone or screen access.

sections.heading: How do you prepare the Companion?
paragraphs: Open it before the interview, select the microphone and computer-output source you intend to use, and confirm that the meters respond. Enter the connection code from the OfferSteady preparation page. If you change a headset or output device, verify the selected route again before continuing.

Start from the Web workspace: create or open the intended interview, continue to preparation, and use the connection code shown there. A successful device connection does not itself start an interview. Review the selected materials and settings before entering the live workspace.

sections.heading: What should you verify on macOS and Windows?
paragraphs: Confirm that the operating system recognises the microphone you selected and that the Companion has the permission required for the feature you intend to use. Screen capture and audio permissions are controlled by the operating system, so a browser permission does not replace a Companion permission.

On any platform, reconnecting a headset can change the active device. Check the microphone and computer-output meters after every device change. If one source is unavailable, do not assume the other source has failed as well; verify them independently.

sections.heading: What can you do if the connection is inactive?
paragraphs: Keep the preparation page open and confirm that the six-digit code belongs to that session. Check network access, the selected sources, and the visible permission state. If the application reports a newer compatible release, use only the verified option shown in the signed-in product.

If audio stops after a device change, reselect the intended route and speak or play a short test while watching the meter. If Screen Assist is the only feature needed, confirm the selected display and capture permission without enabling unrelated audio sources.

sections.heading: Privacy and interview rules
paragraphs: Raw audio is not stored by default. Screenshots are created only when you trigger capture. Follow applicable law and the interview organiser's rules for recording, transcription, screen capture, confidentiality, and AI assistance.
